Entity: Byword / AI Article Generation at Scale
Friction: Byword prices articles à la carte — $99 for 25, $299 for 80, $999 for 300, a near-flat $3.30–$4.00 per article — while the rest of the category sells bundles where the article count is one line among links, visibility tracking and audits. Roundups compare headline prices across those two structures, so buyers either pay bundle prices for articles they could buy alone, or discover the cheap bundle bills in credits, not articles.
Logic: Normalize every candidate to its own billing unit before comparing: Byword sells articles, Outrank sells a 30-article bundle with publishing and links at the same $99, Arvow sells credits where a standard article costs about 10 of its 1,000, Autoblogging.ai sells credit tiers from $19, BabyLoveGrowth sells a four-part bundle. Per-article arithmetic is only honest inside one unit system — cross-unit comparisons must name the unit. The evaluation question is whether you need articles alone (then Byword's free 5-article start is the cheapest test, and its per-article rate is the number to beat) or the jobs around them. We are not an alternative: audit only, no generation.
content_angle: Byword is the only tool in this set that prices per article; everyone else prices per bundle or per credit. The comparison holds each vendor to its own unit system, quotes only first-party pages with verification dates, and treats the UGC-heavy SERP as a symptom worth naming — buyers here distrust vendor claims, so every number carries its source. Names our own position: audit-only, not an alternative.
author: Marcus Orion
